query: Microsoft Alphabet Amazon Meta capital expenditures most recent quarter
normalized: alphabet amazon capital expenditures meta microsoft quarter

output.content:
Using each company’s most recently reported quarter, capital expenditures were: 

| Company | Most recent quarter | Capital expenditures | Definition / disclosure basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Microsoft | FY2026 Q2, ended Dec. 31, 2025 | **$37.5bn** | Capex plus finance leases; this includes **$29.9bn** of cash paid for PP&E and **$6.7bn** of finance leases. [[1]]|
| Alphabet | Q2 2026 | **$44.9bn** | CapEx, with the vast majority directed to technical infrastructure; approximately 60% was servers and 40% data centers/networking. [[2]]|
| Amazon | Q2 2026, ended June 30, 2026 | **$54.2bn** | Cash purchases of property and equipment; Amazon separately reported $0.6bn of equipment acquired under finance leases. [[3]]|
| Meta | Q2 2026 | **$31.08bn** | Capex including principal payments on finance leases. [[4]]|

Amazon was the largest quarterly spender on the cash-purchases measure at **$54.2bn**, followed by Alphabet at **$44.9bn**, Microsoft at **$37.5bn**, and Meta at **$31.1bn**. [[3]] [[2]] [[1]] [[4]] 

The figures are not perfectly like-for-like: Microsoft’s and Meta’s headline measures explicitly include finance-lease-related spending, whereas Amazon’s $54.2bn is purchases of PP&E and Alphabet reports its CapEx figure directly. [[1]] [[4]] [[3]] [[2]]
